div.head: II Cn Prol.
div.ab: Þis is [þonne] seo woruldcunde gerædnes, ðe ic wylle, mid minan witenan ræde, þæt man healde ofer eall Englaland.
Ðis is þonne seo worldcunde geredness, þe ic wille mid minan witenan ræde, þæt man healde ofer eall Englaland.
Hęc est institutio legum secularium, quam communi sapientum meorum consilio per totam Angliam teneri precipio.
Ðis is ðonne seo woruldcunde gerædnysse ðe ic wille, mid minan witenan ræde, þæt man healde ofer eall Englaland.
Þis is seo woruldcunde gerædnes þe ic wylle, mid minan witenan ræde, þæt man healde ofer eall Englaland.
This is further the secular ordinance which, by the advice of my councillors, I desire should be observed over all England.
This is the secular decree which, on the advice of my councilors, I desire to be observed throughout all England.
This is now the secular ordinance which I, with the advice of my councillors, wish to be observed over all England….
Prolog. Dies ist nun die weltliche Verordnung, die ich mit meinem Witanrathe will, dass man über ganz England hin halte.
Prologue. This, then, is the secular ordinance which I will, with the counsel of my witan, that men keep throughout all England.

div.note: Base text K = G (Cotton Nero A I); N = A (Harley 55); B (CCCC 383) is also given here. D (CCCC 201) has 1–4.1 in a reworked form (‘witena gerædnes is …’) after I Cn 2.2. ‘þonne’ is supplied in G from B, A and Ld (compare III Eg 1). Liebermann compares III Eg 1.

I have omitted clauses drawn mainly from VI Ethelred, 8.1–9, since they differ little from V Ethelred, 1.1–1.2, though the source of this, III Edgar, has been used also. These general principles are then followed by prohibitions of too ready application of the death-penalty, and of the sale of men abroad, see V Ethelred, 2, 3. Then VI Ethelred, 7 (see p. 442, n. 2) is repeated.
Manuscripts: A = London, British Library, Harley MS 55, fols. 7v–13v; B = Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 383, pp. 47– 72; G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fols. 16r–41r.
